## Summary

Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.

Fix mixed-case writes before merging because the new setter can make an entry unreachable through the case-insensitive getter.

## Changes

The pull request adds `Cache.set`, raises the default TTL from 60 to 300 seconds, and adds tests for round trips, expiry, and the default TTL constant.

## Critical

- app/cache.py:27 — correctness — Normalize mixed-case keys on write — On a fresh cache, `set("ALPHA", 1)` followed by `get("ALPHA")` returns `None`. The setter stores the original key, while the getter looks up `key.lower()`. — Callers get cache misses after mixed-case writes and can keep reading an older value after a mixed-case update. — Fix: Extend `test_set_then_get_round_trip` with a mixed-case write.

## Important

(none)

## Suggestions

- app/cache.py:27 — correctness — Expire entries at their TTL deadline — With `Cache(ttl=1)`, a value written at monotonic time `1000.0` is still returned at `1001.0`. The setter records `1001.0` as the deadline, and the getter checks `expires < time.monotonic()`. — A read that lands exactly on the deadline can serve stale data. — Fix: Use `expires <= time.monotonic()` at `app/cache.py:21`.
- app/cache.py:7 — comments — Qualify the 300-second expiry as the default — With `Cache(ttl=1)`, an entry uses a one-second TTL despite the comment “Entries expire 300 seconds after they are written.” The setter computes the deadline with `time.monotonic() + self._ttl`. — The comment gives callers using a custom TTL the wrong expectation about how long their entries remain available.
- tests/test_cache.py:18 — tests — Test five-minute expiry through the cache API — If `Cache()` used a 60-second TTL while `Cache.DEFAULT_TTL` remained 300, `test_default_ttl_is_five_minutes` would still pass. It asserts the class constant directly. — A regression that shortens the default entry lifetime could pass the suite.
